reason: A density unit ('6–9 cilia per mm'), not a plant structure. The counted part is the cilium, which is the trichome (PO_0000282; cilia is a synonym) on a margin. This follows 'per cm' and 'per node' in the earlier reviews.

NARROWER. Floras use spicule for a minute, pointed, usually unicellular outgrowth of the epidermis (a prickle-hair), and PO treats bristle, seta and barb trichome as kinds of trichome. 'Tiny ± deltoid' gives the shape quality. Prickle (PO_0025169) is a sclerified emergence of the epidermis, which is too coarse for these minute cells.
A density unit ('1–3 hairs per mm of width'). The counted part is the trichome (PO_0000282). Same reasoning as 'per cm'.
An area-density unit ('21–60 hairs/mm²') that goes with the hairs (trichome, PO_0000282) of some surface. It is not a structure.

NARROWER. This is the axil, the angle between a leaflet (PO_0020049) and the rachis, so it is a specific axil, just as leaf axil (PO_0009023) is. The flora contexts ('leaflet axils and petiole bases hairy') need only the general axil class. A separate class is not justified for 2 floras; leaf vein axil (FLOPO_0986128) is the precedent if one is wanted later.
A fragment ('5 longer ones') that refers back to parts named earlier in the sentence. It is a comparative without its referent, like 'shorter' and 'longer', which the 2026-11-13 review rejected.
The unit of a count ('culms 5–9 per clump'). The counted part is the culm (stem, PO_0009047). This follows 'per plant' and 'per shoot'.
The unit of a count ('perianth appendages 2 per stamen'). This follows 'per flower', 'per bract' and 'per segment'.

The contexts ('cells as in the bracts', 'domelike' cells, 0.2 mm long) are bryophyte descriptions of the cells of the perianth around the archegonia. These are the cells of the gametophyte perianth, not of the angiosperm perianth (PO_0009058). Express this with pattern 'part of a qualified whole': a cell that is part of the gametophyte perianth. The parent should be checked against the moss/liverwort source flora.

In Carex this is the line or slit on the abaxial side of the perigynium beak, often with a hyaline margin. It is a region of an existing FLOPO class, so express it as the abaxial side of the perigynium beak and give the colour or hyaline quality to that region. A suture class is not needed for 2 floras.

A quality: the degree of division of a fern frond ('1(–2)-pinnate-pinnatifid'). In '18–20 pinnate-pinnatifid pairs' the counted part is the pinna (leaflet, PO_0020049). 'Pinnate' was rejected as not a plant structure on 2026-11-13.

NARROWER. These are the ultimate divisions of the branched styles of a pistillate flower (e.g. Croton: 'styles 3, multifid, terminal segments 6–24'). Count them with pattern 03 on style branch. The 'terminal' position could be added with pattern 18 if needed.

Seta is an exact synonym of trichome in PO. These are the bristles on the receptacle of a head (Asteraceae, e.g. Gaillardia), so express them as 'part of a qualified whole' and count or mark them present/absent with pattern 15. PO's receptacle is the flower receptacle; the head's receptacle has no PO class, so the part_of target is approximate. Seta (PO_0030032), the moss sporophyte stalk, does not apply.

target: sepal (PO_0009031), apex region (plant organ apex FLOPO_0985023 of the sepal)
reason: The hood is the hooded (cucullate) upper part of a sepal. Express it as the apex region of the sepal, with the shape qualities ('broadly rounded', 'notched', 'obscure') on that region. Alternatively, record 'cucullate' (FLOPO_0991119) on the sepal. The bare 'hood' was rejected as generic on 2026-11-13; here the qualifier makes it groundable.
A fragment ('5 shorter ones') referring back to parts named earlier. It is a comparative without its referent, as with 'shorter', which was rejected on 2026-11-13.

Ambiguous without the organ. It could be a floral spur (FLOPO_0986133; petal spur PO_0025511), a short shoot (PO_0004701, which has 'spur' as a synonym), or a spur on a fruit or seed ('finely tuberculate', 'swollen tips'). Ground it only when the flora gives the bearing organ.
A ratio phrase ('1–4 times longer than seed'): pattern 10 with seed (PO_0009010) as the reference part. Same as 'times calyx' and 'times tube'.
A ratio phrase ('lobes 2.5–3 times longer than throat'): pattern 10 with corolla throat (FLOPO_0986110) as the reference part. Same as 'times tube'.
The second term of a length ratio ('petiole 1/4–1/2 total leaf length'): pattern 10 with the leaf as the reference. Same as 'calyx length' and 'leaf length'.

target: leaf lamina vein (PO_0020138), at a position (basal, basiscopic side of the pinna costa)
reason: Fern veins (e.g. Thelypteridaceae) at the base of a segment on the basiscopic side. Count them with pattern 14 (count at a position) on leaf lamina vein. The position words do not need a class.

'Calli' was rejected as a generic part on 2026-11-13. 'Bifid' is a quality, not part of the name. If the orchid lip calli keep coming back, the remedy is a 'labellum callus' class, not this phrase. Plant callus (PO_0005052) is tissue-culture callus and does not apply.
'Circular' is a quality (PATO), and 'scar' needs the organ that left it: leaf scar FLOPO_0986052, pedicel scar FLOPO_0986113 or stipule scar FLOPO_0986116. The examples do not say which.
Same as 'bifid calli': the generic 'calli' (rejected 2026-11-13) with a shape quality attached.
Generic crests ('apical cristae 4–12', 'with 2 cristae'). The bearing organ (seed, fruit, lip, anther) is not given, so it cannot be grounded.
NARROWER. In bamboos the culm bud is the branch bud in the axil of a culm sheath at a culm node. It is a vegetative axillary bud, and 'culm bud 1' is a count per node.
The stalk bearing a Fagaceae cupule ('rachis and cupule stalks grayish scurfy'). Both classes exist, so this is the 'part of a qualified whole' pattern.
A count phrase ('1 flower per axil'). The counted part is the flower (PO_0009046) and the unit is the axil. Same as 'per axil' and 'per leaf axil'.

A count phrase ('palea with 5–40 hooks per keel'). 'Hook' was rejected as generic on 2026-11-14, and the keel is the unit. These hooks are hooked prickle-hairs (trichome, PO_0000282) on the palea (PO_0009038) keels, which can be expressed with pattern 14.
Same as 'bifid calli': the generic 'calli' (rejected 2026-11-13) with a shape quality (lamellate) attached.

target: labellum lobe (FLOPO_0986028), lateral position (pattern 18), margin region
reason: The margin of a lateral lobe of the orchid lip (orchid labellum FLOPO_0980978). The lobe class exists, the position is pattern 18, and the margin is a region; crisped, ciliate and erose go on that region. Note that config/flopo_positioned_parts.tsv lists 'lip' as a narrow synonym of lower petal (FLOPO_0996024). In orchid floras 'lip' should go to the labellum instead.
